Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

Reviewing a company’s long-term sales performance reveals insights into its quality. Any business can have short-term success, but a top-tier one grows for years.

This also enables it to gain more leverage on its fixed costs than smaller competitors and the flexibility to offer lower prices. However, its scale is a double-edged sword because it’s harder to find incremental growth when you’ve penetrated most of the market. What Is the Market Really Paying for Jabil’s (JBL) Growth?
Jabil (NYSE:JBL) has evolved into a high-margin advanced manufacturing powerhouse, shifting away from low-margin assembly toward AI infrastructure, healthcare, and high-complexity hardware. The company's underlying fundamentals highlight exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by a core return on invested capital that expanded to 59% in fiscal 2026 while sustaining aggressive share repurchases. Even as Jabil expands its footprint, could a major rival's massive multi-billion-dollar play in AI power infrastructure siphon market share away? Click to find out.
What Is the Market Really Paying for Jabil's (JBL) Growth?
Jabil has spent years shedding its image as a plain contract manufacturer, and its Sept. 30, 2026 earnings call made the case that the makeover is paying off. Fourth-quarter revenue jumped 29% year over year, and core earnings per share rose 34% to $4.40. Management then guided fiscal 2027 core EPS to $17.55, another gain of about 34%. The business is clearly accelerating, but what investors are willing to pay for that acceleration is the more interesting story. Yet, as hardware demand surges across hyperscale networks, will another key supplier steal the spotlight in optical connectivity after a major sector giant's recent plunge? Read more here.
The engine is AI infrastructure. Jabil generated $14.4 billion of AI-related revenue in fiscal 2026 and expects $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, a 54% increase. What makes that easier to believe is where the demand comes from. Management says most of it supports inference, the everyday running of existing models, rather than the race to train frontier systems, and direct exposure to frontier developers is a small fraction. Usage-driven demand needs storage, networking, power, and cooling, not just accelerators, and Jabil now builds across all of it. Six customers in the segment are expected to top $1 billion each in fiscal 2027.
The second leg is how efficiently growth turns into cash. Jabil supported $36.0 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026 on just $470 million of net capital spending, which is why core return on invested capital sits at 59%, nearly triple the fiscal 2020 level. Free cash flow beat the company's own early target, and management plans to return at least 80% of it to shareholders over time. Buybacks absorbed about $1.1 billion of that in fiscal 2026.
Growth at this pace has to be physically built, and supply is the choke point. Francis McKay, the chief supply chain officer, said memory is being pulled toward AI and hyperscale buyers, squeezing the other markets Jabil serves. That already shows up in guidance, where Connected Living is expected to shrink 15% to $2.3 billion, partly because management is cautious about memory and partly because it is exiting lower-complexity programs. Healthcare also fell short of expectations in the fourth quarter, thanks to equipment delays and a customer program that slipped.
Execution and concentration come next. Jabil is adding more than $8.5 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, which management itself called unprecedented, and a second hyperscale customer is expected to pass 10% of total revenue, a mark only one customer reached two years ago. Net inventory days of 64 still sit above the 55 to 60 day target, so working capital has to tighten while the factories scale. Management also raised the question of AI volatility on the call, arguing that its inference-heavy mix is steadier.
Hedge fund interest ticked higher, with 69 funds holding Jabil against 67 in the prior quarter, so institutions are adding rather than heading for the exits. Short interest of 3.24% of float is low, which signals little organized betting against the story. The forward P/E of 19.34, as of October 2, is where the real debate sits. Earnings are guided to grow about 34% in fiscal 2027, so a multiple under 20 leaves little growth premium in the price, and the market appears to want proof before paying for it. Is that caution fair? An inference-heavy mix and a share count cut by 49% since fiscal 2013 argue for some support under the stock. But a modest multiple only looks cheap if the earnings arrive, and memory supply and the capacity buildout are the two things that could delay them.
Jabil's story comes down to whether its new factory space fills on schedule. The evidence shows a company growing fast, generating cash and trading at a multiple that does not demand perfection. Bulls need committed customer programs to keep ramping into the capacity already built. Bears need only a memory shortage or a stumbled launch to show how much.

Jabil’s Double-Beat and Raise Is a Signal That This Rally Will Continue
Thomas Hughes - MarketBeat - Thu Oct 1, 8:45AM CDT
Tepid market response or not, Jabil’s (NYSE: JBL) recent double-beat earnings report was a buy signal, reinforcing the thesis that has driven shares thus far and strengthening the forward outlook.
AI is driving a surge in demand across the company's product lines, pointing to a sustained upcycle and cash-generating capacity.
Cash-generating capacity is the core thesis, as Jabil is the muscle behind more prominent names such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), converting demand for their products into reality.
Jabil’s dividend is a token, yielding less than 0.25%, intended mainly to keep dividend-only funds and institutions in the mix. The firm aggressively repurchases shares and can continue doing so next year.
Highlights from its last fiscal year include about $1 billion in repurchases, up year over year and sufficient to reduce the share count by 3.6%, and a free cash flow payout ratio of about 69%.
Looking ahead, management forecasts free cash flow growth in the coming year, signaling capacity for accelerated buybacks and greater shareholder leverage, which may provide an incentive to buy shares at current levels.
Jabil Boosted by AI, Shows Strengths in All Categories
Jabil posted a solid quarter, with revenue accelerating sequentially and year over year (YOY) to nearly 29%, the fastest pace in more than five years. Revenue growth also outpaced the consensus by a wide margin, approximately 900 basis points (bps), driven by 56% growth in Intelligent Infrastructure. Intelligent Infrastructure did the heavy lifting, but was not the only segment to show strength, with Regulated Industries up by 9% and Connected Living/Digital Commerce flat. CEO Mike Dastoor also highlighted several end markets not related to the data center and AI infrastructure, including automotive, healthcare, energy, defense, aerospace, and warehouse automation.
Margin news was another bright spot. The company faced cost pressures and gross margin headwinds, but they were less than expected and offset by operational quality. Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased at a much slower pace than revenue growth, showing that Jabil is becoming more efficient as it grows, which helped earnings rise faster than revenue. Adjusted earnings per share rose nearly 34% YOY to $4.40, outpacing top-line growth by about 500 bps, with strengths expected to carry into the coming year.
Guidance is a key reason the stock price uptrend is likely to continue. Jabil’s guidance for the next quarter and year is hot on all counts, with revenue and earnings expected to be well above MarketBeat’s reported consensus. The likely outcome is that JBL continues to build momentum, running at the high end of its expected range if not exceeding it, and lifting the year-end outlook along the way.
Analysts Caution Triggers Buying Opportunity in Jabil Shares
Analysts were generally bullish following Jabil’s release, highlighting the revenue strength and earnings quality, but took a cautious stance, focusing on back-end margin expansion and the upfront cost of its capacity buildout. No analysts revised a price target or altered sentiment immediately following the report, leaving the trend unchanged.
The trend includes steady coverage, a Buy consensus with 90% Buy-side bias, and a forecast for nearly 50% upside relative to Q3’s support levels and a fresh all-time high. More importantly, JBL trades well below the lowest analyst price target, signaling a deep-value opportunity and potential for explosive upside as stronger catalysts emerge.
Institutions are likewise bullish on Jabil's stock, citing its cash flow, capital returns, and underlying demand for its clients' products. They own more than 90% of the shares, have bought aggressively over the trailing 12 months, and ramped activity in Q3, reaching a record peak.
JBL’s price action reflects a bullish market posture. The stock is up more than 35% YOY and more than 100% over the past two years, with the 2026 pullback offering value relative to recent peaks. A deeper pullback is possible, but strong support is evident as September comes to a close, so the risk is minimal. The likely scenario is that JBL remains close to this level until more news becomes available, likely in upcoming earnings reports.
The market may not be getting JBL’s report wrong so much as the price action reflects the split between short-term traders and long-term investors. Short-term traders focus on near-term bottlenecks, AI fears, and capacity costs, and fail to price in the impact on long-term cash flow. Long-term traders, focused on cash flow, capital returns, and capital gains, can easily look past upfront costs and focus on the demand curve, which is improving quarterly across numerous end markets, not just AI.
Jabil’s biggest risk now is executional. Investors need the company's strategy to progress without hiccups, which are likely, given the advanced nature of AI hardware and industry-wide bottlenecks.

Jabil Inc. stock (ISIN US46612W1036) is trading near USD 300 on September 14, 2026 after the electronics manufacturing specialist reported double-digit revenue growth and better-than-expected earnings for Q3 of fiscal 2026, while several analysts raised or reiterated bullish price targets on the shares.
Q3 FY2026 results beat forecasts and lift guidance
According to Investing.com, Jabil posted Q3 FY2026 revenue of USD 8.8 billion, an increase of 12.0 percent year on year and above the USD 8.55 billion consensus forecast for the quarter, underscoring robust demand across its end markets in the three months to around mid-2026.
In the same Q3 FY2026 period, Jabil delivered earnings per share of USD 3.16, coming in USD 0.08 above the estimated USD 3.08 and signaling continued operating leverage as volumes grow.Investing.com Management reported a core operating margin of 5.8 percent for Q3 FY2026, and indicated that margins are expected to expand above 6.0 percent in fiscal 2027 as higher-value AI-related business scales.
AI revenue and cash flow outlook support the stock
The Q3 FY2026 update also highlighted how artificial-intelligence infrastructure is becoming a central driver for Jabil. Jabil now expects AI-related revenue of about USD 13.6 billion in fiscal 2026, representing roughly 50.0 percent growth versus the prior year and USD 0.5 billion above the company’s outlook from March 2026.Investing.com For investors, this accelerating AI exposure is an important part of the equity story because it supports both growth and margin expansion.
Jabil also raised its adjusted free cash flow guidance for fiscal 2026 to more than USD 1.4 billion, up from a previous target of USD 1.3 billion, giving the company greater scope for shareholder returns and balance-sheet flexibility.Investing.com At the same time, inventory days stood at 84 days versus a medium-term target range of 55 to 60 days, illustrating that supply-chain constraints and elevated working capital remain key risks even against the positive growth backdrop.
Analysts highlight upside potential with higher price targets
Analyst commentary has turned increasingly constructive in recent days. In an overview of recent recommendations, TipRanks reports that Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy rating on Jabil on September 14, 2026 with a price target of USD 375.00 per share, while UBS reiterated its own Buy rating with a higher target of USD 430.00 per share.
Another analyst round-up shows that Jabil currently carries a Strong Buy consensus, with an average price target of USD 438.25 that implies about 42.7 percent upside relative to recent levels, and notes that in a report dated August 30, 2026 Goldman Sachs had previously set a more ambitious USD 482.00 target.TipRanks For retail investors, these figures quantify how much optimism is already embedded in the stock and how sensitive sentiment may be to any disappointment in upcoming quarters.
Next earnings date and what investors will watch
Looking ahead, the next major checkpoint for Jabil Inc. stock is the upcoming release of fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results. Jabil is scheduled to report its next earnings on September 30, 2026, with a related webcast planned that morning.TradingView Both Investing.com data and Yahoo Finance’s earnings calendar list September 30, 2026 as the next earnings date, underlining its importance as the next fundamental driver for the shares.
Given the raised guidance and the ambitious analyst targets, investors are likely to focus on whether Jabil can sustain double-digit revenue growth into Q4 FY2026 and fiscal 2027, keep core operating margins moving above 6.0 percent, and continue to convert earnings into strong free cash flow. Any sign that AI demand is slowing or that inventory levels are not normalizing could challenge the current valuation, especially with the consensus already pricing in sizable upside.
Jabil Inc. stock price and trading context
Per recent NYSE data cited by Investing.com, Jabil Inc. stock last traded at about USD 298.62 on the New York Stock Exchange in mid-September 2026, with the shares previously closing at USD 318.08 on an earlier session that had seen a gain of roughly 5.05 percent.Investing.com This places the stock below its consensus price targets from major houses such as Goldman Sachs and UBS, but still after a strong run following the Q3 FY2026 earnings release.

Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

Jabil's Fiscal 2027 Outlook Leaves Room for Upside, UBS Says
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 9:59 AM PDT 1 min read
Jabil's (JBL) initial fiscal 2027 outlook looks cautious given management's history of guiding low and then beating, so the market is likely to underwrite higher estimates, UBS Securities said.
The brokerage said in a note Wednesday that the company started fiscal 2025 and 2026 roughly 10% and 15% above its initial revenue guides, respectively, and expects investors to assume at least 10% upside to the $44.5 billion fiscal 2027 revenue guide, or about $49 billion.
Stronger volume should also leave room for operating margin to expand 10 to 20 basis points beyond the initial 6.1% guide, UBS said. It expects the market to underwrite EPS of at least $20, versus the $17.55 guide.
The investment firm raised its fiscal 2027 earnings per share estimate to $17.57 from $16.78 and its fiscal 2028 estimate to $22.63 from $20.24. It cited stronger AI-related demand. Jabil also raised its fiscal 2027 AI-related revenue growth outlook to 54% from about 50%.
UBS kept its buy rating and $430 price target.
Shares of Jabil were up 3.4% in Thursday afternoon trading.

Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

Jabil’s Double-Beat and Raise Is a Signal That This Rally Will Continue
Thomas Hughes - MarketBeat - Thu Oct 1, 8:45AM CDT
Tepid market response or not, Jabil’s (NYSE: JBL) recent double-beat earnings report was a buy signal, reinforcing the thesis that has driven shares thus far and strengthening the forward outlook.
AI is driving a surge in demand across the company's product lines, pointing to a sustained upcycle and cash-generating capacity.
Cash-generating capacity is the core thesis, as Jabil is the muscle behind more prominent names such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), converting demand for their products into reality.
Jabil’s dividend is a token, yielding less than 0.25%, intended mainly to keep dividend-only funds and institutions in the mix. The firm aggressively repurchases shares and can continue doing so next year.
Highlights from its last fiscal year include about $1 billion in repurchases, up year over year and sufficient to reduce the share count by 3.6%, and a free cash flow payout ratio of about 69%.
Looking ahead, management forecasts free cash flow growth in the coming year, signaling capacity for accelerated buybacks and greater shareholder leverage, which may provide an incentive to buy shares at current levels.
Jabil Boosted by AI, Shows Strengths in All Categories
Jabil posted a solid quarter, with revenue accelerating sequentially and year over year (YOY) to nearly 29%, the fastest pace in more than five years. Revenue growth also outpaced the consensus by a wide margin, approximately 900 basis points (bps), driven by 56% growth in Intelligent Infrastructure. Intelligent Infrastructure did the heavy lifting, but was not the only segment to show strength, with Regulated Industries up by 9% and Connected Living/Digital Commerce flat. CEO Mike Dastoor also highlighted several end markets not related to the data center and AI infrastructure, including automotive, healthcare, energy, defense, aerospace, and warehouse automation.
Margin news was another bright spot. The company faced cost pressures and gross margin headwinds, but they were less than expected and offset by operational quality. Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased at a much slower pace than revenue growth, showing that Jabil is becoming more efficient as it grows, which helped earnings rise faster than revenue. Adjusted earnings per share rose nearly 34% YOY to $4.40, outpacing top-line growth by about 500 bps, with strengths expected to carry into the coming year.
Guidance is a key reason the stock price uptrend is likely to continue. Jabil’s guidance for the next quarter and year is hot on all counts, with revenue and earnings expected to be well above MarketBeat’s reported consensus. The likely outcome is that JBL continues to build momentum, running at the high end of its expected range if not exceeding it, and lifting the year-end outlook along the way.
Analysts Caution Triggers Buying Opportunity in Jabil Shares
Analysts were generally bullish following Jabil’s release, highlighting the revenue strength and earnings quality, but took a cautious stance, focusing on back-end margin expansion and the upfront cost of its capacity buildout. No analysts revised a price target or altered sentiment immediately following the report, leaving the trend unchanged.
The trend includes steady coverage, a Buy consensus with 90% Buy-side bias, and a forecast for nearly 50% upside relative to Q3’s support levels and a fresh all-time high. More importantly, JBL trades well below the lowest analyst price target, signaling a deep-value opportunity and potential for explosive upside as stronger catalysts emerge.
Institutions are likewise bullish on Jabil's stock, citing its cash flow, capital returns, and underlying demand for its clients' products. They own more than 90% of the shares, have bought aggressively over the trailing 12 months, and ramped activity in Q3, reaching a record peak.
JBL’s price action reflects a bullish market posture. The stock is up more than 35% YOY and more than 100% over the past two years, with the 2026 pullback offering value relative to recent peaks. A deeper pullback is possible, but strong support is evident as September comes to a close, so the risk is minimal. The likely scenario is that JBL remains close to this level until more news becomes available, likely in upcoming earnings reports.
The market may not be getting JBL’s report wrong so much as the price action reflects the split between short-term traders and long-term investors. Short-term traders focus on near-term bottlenecks, AI fears, and capacity costs, and fail to price in the impact on long-term cash flow. Long-term traders, focused on cash flow, capital returns, and capital gains, can easily look past upfront costs and focus on the demand curve, which is improving quarterly across numerous end markets, not just AI.
Jabil’s biggest risk now is executional. Investors need the company's strategy to progress without hiccups, which are likely, given the advanced nature of AI hardware and industry-wide bottlenecks.

Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.
